Stratified Models

Six experiments to explore and review

Follow graph regularization from coefficient fields to classification, optimization, streaming data, and reusable fitted artifacts. These hosted notebooks show saved, executed quick-run outputs. Treat their controls as read-only. Live sliders, reruns, original-data reproductions, and full-size presets require a Python server with marimo and JAX. The local instructions below open that experience. Review pull request #5 · Notebook guide · Source snapshot 39f8289

Choose a notebook

01 · Graph regression

See how graph structure, regularization, and a missing training group shape coefficients and held-out error. Compare pooled, independent, and stratified fits against known truth.

02 · Mesothelioma classification

Review probability estimates, held-out scores, and age/sex coefficient curves. The quick run is synthetic; the source includes an explicit original-data, paper-method protocol.

03 · Spatial house prices

Inspect spatial coefficient maps and log-price errors against pooled and separate models. The synthetic quick run introduces the full paper-method preset available in the source.

04 · Solver diagnostics and reuse

Compare eligible solvers on the same objective. Inspect ADMM residual thresholds, numerical certificates, typed nonconvergence, warm starts, and shared numerical caches.

05 · Streaming and composition

Follow one data snapshot through in-memory and batched fitting with pandas, Polars, or Parquet. Compare results, explicit preprocessing, bin boundaries, and data-replay costs.

06 · From experiment to artifact

Review discrimination and calibration, fold-isolated tuning, sklearn cloning, and versioned prediction artifacts. See fitted components round-trip and failures stay explicit.

Run with live controls

Install uv, then run these commands in a terminal. They select the implementation revision used for this review. 
git clone https://github.com/tomshlomo/stratified-models.git
cd stratified-models
git checkout 39f8289a3631e0477735450c2e7f731fb305ac2e
uv sync --frozen --extra common --group dev
uv run --extra common marimo run examples/01_graph_regression.py
Open the local address printed by marimo. Change the final filename to explore another notebook. Use marimo edit instead of marimo run to inspect or change its Python cells. Larger experiments and external data downloads require explicit actions inside the notebooks. Paper reproduction protocols · Browse the six notebook sources
